preparation: Avoid high-dose biotin supplements (more than 5 mg/day) for at least 8 hours before blood collection

faqs.question: What does the Calcitonin Test measure?
faqs.answer: It measures the level of calcitonin hormone in your blood, produced by thyroid C-cells.

faqs.question: Why is this test done?
faqs.answer: It helps diagnose and monitor medullary thyroid carcinoma and C-cell hyperplasia

faqs.question: Do I need to fast before the test?
Can supplements affect my results?
faqs.answer: Yes, high doses of biotin can interfere with results; stop taking them 8 hours before your test.

faqs.question: What are normal calcitonin levels?
faqs.answer: Typically below 10.2 pg/mL, though normal ranges may vary slightly by lab.

faqs.question: What does a high calcitonin level mean?
faqs.answer: It may suggest medullary thyroid carcinoma, C-cell hyperplasia, or other conditions such as chronic liver disease.

faqs.question: How is the test performed?
faqs.answer: A simple blood sample is drawn from a vein in your arm and analysed using ECLIA.

faqs.question: When will I get my report?
faqs.answer: Reports are usually ready within 8 hours after the sample reaches the lab.
